description: Ex-Marineflieger Sea Hawk Mk 101 all-weather fighter displayed outdoors in Bundesmarine markings RB+363. Sea Hawks equipped Marinefliegergeschwader 1 and 2 from 1958. Present in the outdoor park as of 2024 photographs.
aliases: Sea Hawk Mk100; SeaHawk; Hawker Sea Hawk

description: Ex-Indian Navy Sea Hawk wearing Indian Navy serial IN238; acquired to represent the Marineflieger Sea Hawk fleet alongside RB+363. Outdoor display, confirmed present 2024.
Ex-Marineflieger Fairey Gannet AS.4 anti-submarine aircraft in Bundesmarine markings UA+113. Gannets served with Marinefliegergeschwader 3 at Nordholz itself. Outdoor display, confirmed 2024.
Ex-Marineflieger Atlantic in the SIGINT configuration, noted for the African wildlife motif applied to its fin. Delivered to the museum from Nordholz air base; outdoor display, confirmed 2024.
Ex-Marinefliegergeschwader Tornado IDS, one of two Tornados at the museum; both came from the disbanded naval Tornado wings at Eggebek and Jagel. Outdoor display, confirmed 2024.
Second Tornado IDS at the Aeronauticum, displayed in a different colour scheme from 43+55. Outdoor display, confirmed 2024.
Ex-Luftwaffe F-104G Starfighter displayed outdoors. Retains Bundeswehr code 20+64.
Ex-Marineflieger F-104G Starfighter, licence-built by Messerschmitt; the Marineflieger operated the Starfighter in the anti-shipping role from Eggebek and Jagel. Outdoor display, confirmed 2024.
Ex-NVA/Luftstreitkräfte der DDR Su-22M4, taken over by the Bundeswehr in 1990 and displayed here in its East German tactical number 366.
Fouga CM.170 Magister jet trainer displayed in Bundeswehr markings SC+601; the airframe also carries the number 388 from earlier French service.
Ex-Luftwaffe Percival Pembroke C.54 light transport, a type used for communications and covert photographic flights. Outdoor display.
Ex-Marineflieger Do 28 D-2 Skyservant, one of three Skyservants at the museum. Outdoor display.
Second ex-Marineflieger Do 28 D-2 Skyservant at the Aeronauticum. Outdoor display.
Third ex-Marineflieger Do 28 D-2 Skyservant at the Aeronauticum. Outdoor display.
Ex-Heeresflieger Sikorsky H-34G.III transport helicopter, licence-built by Sud-Aviation. Outdoor display.
aliases: H34; S-58; Choctaw; H-34G; H34G.III; S58; H34G

description: Ex-Luftwaffe Piaggio P.149D basic trainer and liaison aircraft, licence-built in Germany by Focke-Wulf. Outdoor display.
Ex-NVA Mi-8S VIP transport helicopter taken over by the Bundeswehr in 1990 and given the code 94+01. Interior fitted out in the East German government configuration.
aliases: Mi8S; Mi-8S; Hip; Mi-8 Salon; Mi8

description: Ex-NVA Mi-8TB armed transport helicopter taken over by the Bundeswehr in 1990 as 94+14. Outdoor display alongside the VIP Mi-8.

Ex-Flugbereitschaft BMVg VFW 614 short-haul jet, one of three used as government transports; cabin accessible to visitors and licensed since 2005 as a venue for civil wedding ceremonies. Bundeswehr code 17+03 also carried.
Bristol Sycamore Mk 52 helicopter in civil marks D-HALC; the type served the Bundeswehr in the search and rescue role before passing to civil owners.

Ship-borne floatplane recovered from the heavy cruiser Prinz Eugen, on long-term loan from the Smithsonian National Air and Space Museum since 2012 and under long-running restoration in the museum workshop; not normally on public display. Werknummer 623183.
